body_text:
A *Laurent series* centered at $z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$ is a bi-infinite series:
$$ \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} a_n (z - z_0)^n = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{a_{-n}}{(z - z_0)^n} + \sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n (z - z_0)^n. $$
If $f$ is holomorphic on an open annulus $A(z_0, r, R) = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : r < |z - z_0| < R\}$
(where $0 \le r < R \le \infty$), it admits a unique Laurent expansion converging absolutely on the
annulus and uniformly on every closed concentric sub-annulus.

The coefficients $a_n$ are given for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ by the contour integral:
$$ a_n = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \oint_\gamma \frac{f(z)}{(z - z_0)^{n+1}}\,dz, $$
where $\gamma$ is any positively oriented circle $|z - z_0| = \rho$ with $r < \rho < R$.
The series of negative powers $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_{-n} (z - z_0)^{-n}$ is the *principal part*,
while the non-negative powers form the *analytic part*.
